lawyer:
Md Imam Hasan, Advocate—For the Petitioner
ASM Abdur Razzaque, Advocate—For the Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Elited Iron and Steel GP Sheet Limited---------------Petitioner
vs
Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Gazipur and another Respondents
full_judgment:
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the Order No. 23 dated 8-1-2023 (Annexure-K) passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1. Gazipur in Artha Execution Case No. 24 of 2018 setting aside the earlier order dated 14-11-2022 allowing the application under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure restoring the execution case in its original file and number should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 2. Relevant facts leading to issuance of the Rule Nisi are that the respondent No. 2, namely, Uttara Bank Limited ("the Bank") obtained a decree against the petitioner and others on 10-9-2009 by filing Artha Rin Suit No. 187 of 2005 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka for Taka 22,88,01,119.77 as on 24-7-2005 with interest till realisation. Pursuant to the said decree the Bank filed Artha Execution Case No. 167 of 2009 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka for realisation of the decretal dues and subsequently the Artha Execution Case was transferred to the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Gazipur and renumbered as Artha Execution Case No. 24 of 2018 inasmuch as the mortgaged property is situated within the local/territorial jurisdiction of Gazipur District Judge. The said Execution case was dismissed for default by order dated 14-11-2022 for not taking step by the decree-holder Bank. Subsequently, the Bank filed an application on 28-11-2022 under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (shortly, "the Act, 2003") read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (shortly, "the Code") for restoration of the said execution case stating explanation for the default. The Adalat by the impugned order dated 8-1-2023 allowed the said application and restored the execution case to its file and number which led the petitioner to file this writ petition. 

 3. Mr Md Imam Hasan, learned Advocate for the petitioner after placing the writ petition and other materials on record submits that the execution case having been dismissed for default the decree-holder bank was left with the remedy under section 28(3) of the Act, 2003 by filing 2nd Execution Case but without resorting to the said provision, on misconception he filed the application for restoration. He further submits that since the Act provides specific provision under section 28(3) of the Act, 2003, there is no scope to file an application under section 57 of the Act, 2003 and, as such, the impugned order entertaining the said application is misconceived. In support of his submissions, learned Advocate refers to the case of Sonali Bank, Sadarghat Corporate Branch, Dhaka vs Mrs Hazera Islam and others, reported in 6 ADC 957, Golden Re-Rolling Industries Ltd. vs Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka and another, reported in 12 MLR (AD) 233 = 60 DLR (AD) 38, Reazul Hogue Molla vs Afizullah Mollah @ Shafiuddin Molla & others, reported in 42 DLR (AD) 74, Janata Bank Ltd. vs Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary Ministry of Finance and Planning and others, reported in 20 BLC 751. 

 5. Controverting the submissions of learned Advocate for the petitioner, Mr ASM Abdur Razzaque, learned Advocate for the respondent No. 2-Bank by filing Affidavit-in-Opposition and Supplementary Affidavit thereto contends that the execution case was filed in the year 2009 and in the meantime the judgment-debtor filed Writ Petitions No. 5099 of 2009, 822 of 2010, 10357 of 2017 and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2409 of 2014 due to which the execution case could not be proceeded in view of interim order passed in the above mentioned litigations and thus the duration of execution case became more than 6 years crossing limitation border under section 28(4) of the Act, 2003. He further contends that due to expiry of 6 years limitation under section 28(4) of the Act, 2003 decree-holder Bank did not have any option to file 2nd execution case. He also contends that due to bonafide reasons the execution case was dismissed for default and within 14 days thereafter, the Bank filed the application for restoration under section 57 of the Act, 2003. He again contends that there is no specific provision in the Act, 2003 for restoration of the execution case and so, section 57 was applied by the Artha Rin Adalat. In support of his submissions, learned Advocate refers to the case of Jahangir Kabir Chowdhury vs Bangladesh Government, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Law Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Bangladesh and others, reported in 22 BLC (AD) 139 and Rizwan Ahmed vs Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka and others, reported in 72 DLR 397. 

 8. According to the aforesaid provision the legislature has incorporated the time-frame for filing the execution case. As per section 28(3) there is scope to file 2nd execution case upon dismissal or disposal of the first execution case within 1 year and section 28(4) clearly makes the total time-line of 6(six) years from the date of filing to first execution case to any subsequent execution case(s). 

 9. From the above provision, it is apparent that the decree-holder can file 2nd execution case on dismissal of execution case for any reasons but that, would within 6 years from the date of filing the 1st execution case. 

 10. Here in this case, the execution case was dismissed not on merit but due to default of decree-holder bank in not taking step and in the Act, there is no specific provision like the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the execution case. Section 57 of the Act, 2003 has been incorporated by the legislature to come forward to aid the litigant(s) under such circumstances to secure ends of justice. Although the decree-holder-Bank had the scope to go for 2nd execution case but he is debarred here due to expiry of 6 years and so he has opted to resort section 57 of the Act, 2003 exercising inherent power of the Court. In this connection, we find support from the case reported in 22 BLC (AD) 139 where the apex Court held as under: 

 11. We have also gone through the case cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. In those cases, it appears that the apex Court held section 57 of the Act, 2003 shall not be applied where the specific provision is provided in the Act and in those cited cases, the application was filed under section 57 of the Act, 2003 in spite of having specific provision of section 32 and section 19 of the Act, 2003. As such, those cited cases are not applicable in this particular case inasmuch as in the Act, 2003 there is no specific provision for restoration of the execution case when it is dismissed for default.
